findings.title: Count likely includes archived/deleted projects, so customers could be overbilled
findings.explanation: The query counts every row in `projects` for the org. The neighboring `activeProjectNames` function suggests the table has an active/inactive distinction (archived, deleted, or status), and its query presumably filters on it. This one does not, so archived or soft-deleted projects would be billed under the new per-project pricing. Decide what 'billable' means with product/billing and apply the same filter (e.g. `AND archived_at IS NULL` or `status = 'active'`). Ideally share one predicate or constant with `activeProjectNames` so the two cannot drift apart.

findings.title: No tests for billing-critical logic
findings.explanation: This number drives invoices. Add tests covering an org with no projects, active projects, archived/deleted projects, and projects belonging to other orgs, so that the billable definition is pinned down and regressions are caught.

findings.title: Comment does not define 'billable'
findings.explanation: 'One billable unit per project' does not say which projects count (active only? trial or free projects? projects created mid-billing-period?). Document the rule. Also consider whether the invoice generator needs a count as of a point in time (billing period) rather than the current count. A live count can change between calculation and invoicing, and it ignores projects that were created or removed during the period.

findings.title: Query formatting inconsistent with existing function
findings.explanation: The existing query is formatted across multiple lines, while this one is a long single line. Consider matching the existing style for readability, and adding an index on `projects(org_id)` if one does not already exist.
